approach: Count the rejected, failed or timed-out jobs of one retry lineage (a chain of "try again on <job>" requests) from the job records, using `job_history` and `retries_by_job` in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs`. The limit is a named constant `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 3`. A core function `lineage_stop(s)` returns None below 3. At 3 or more it returns the failed ids, the findings that repeated and a `NarrowerAction` (Queued existing marker, Queue new text, or Refused). The drain enforces it in two places. (1) In `Drain::prepare`, next to the existing `paused` ask, one batch `Steps::lineage_stops` call over the whole queue: an item whose lineage is already at 3 is not read for planning and is held back like a paused item, then the narrower request is queued and the tripping, still-Queued retry item is dropped with `Athena::close`. (2) In `Drain::attempts` right after `failures += 1`: an item whose own attempt makes the lineage 3 stops before its next attempt. Repeats are matched with the scope guard's T4 normalisation for unmet criteria, and with a stricter stop-word-aware rule for findings so short common words cannot pair different findings. A hand `athena retry` stays unlimited. A new `lineage-limit` default is added, with `buy-first` split to hold the reader prompt at its recorded size. Round-4 changes: the planning-pass hold and the drop of the tripping item (findings 1 and 2), a per-run once-per-lineage guard for concurrent workers (finding 3), a stricter finding matcher (finding 4), and a corrected reason about `retries_by_job` (finding 5). The earlier loop-top check is removed because `prepare` now covers what it covered (decision 1).

decisions.choice: Enforce at two places and drop the earlier loop-top check. (1) Planning hold: in `Drain::prepare` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:2084-2279), right after `paused` is computed (2126-2129), ask one batch `self.steps.lineage_stops(&ids)` for every item in `view.items`. An item that is paused keeps its pause text (pause wins). Any other item with a stop is skipped in the read loop (beside `paused.contains_key`, 2136) and added to `held` (2202) with a lineage reason; the dependents message (2215) says `its retry lineage is stopped` for those and keeps `its line is paused` for paused ones, so the asserts at tests/drain.rs:996 and 1278 are unchanged. `prepare` also stores each stop in a new `State.lineage_held: BTreeMap<String, LineageStop>`. (2) Own-attempt stop: in `Drain::attempts`, right after `failures += 1` (1941), when `passed.is_none()` and `paused_reason(item)` is None, ask `lineage_stops(&[last_job])`; on a stop call `Drain::narrow` and return the new `ItemEnd::LineageStopped(reason)`, which `finish` passes over with the reason.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: `prepare` already reads every unread item whose plan is incomplete, and it skips paused items so they are not read (2124-2138). A bare `try again on <job>` has no acceptance bullets, so its entry is incomplete and it would be read, and paid for, before any `attempts` check. Holding it in `prepare` is the same route the scope guard uses, and its existing test asserts that nothing is read (tests/drain.rs:5527-5534). Point 2 runs after every failure of an item, so a lineage that becomes 3 on the item's first or second attempt is stopped before the next attempt or before the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` return. The old loop-top check is dropped: `prepare` is rebuilt before each wave (drain.rs:3022-3025, 3069), so a queued item at 3 is held before it starts, and point 2 covers every failure inside a run. A check with no test that can tell it from those two would be dead code. `athena plan` calls the same `prepare` (3222), so it shows the hold too, but `prepare` queues and drops nothing: that is done only by the drain, in `queue_lineage_narrowers`, called right after `prepare` at 3002 and 3069.

rejected.option: Keep the loop-top check as well
rejected.why: Nothing reaches it that `prepare` or point 2 has not already stopped, and no test can show it alone.
A queued retry item whose chain is at 3 would be read for planning (a paid Reader call) before any attempt check (finding 1).
`athena plan` calls `prepare` and runs nothing (drain.rs:3211-3222); a planning command must not write records.
It would block the operator's own `athena retry`, the manual override.

decisions.choice: `lineage_attempts(records, job)` in retry.rs calls `job_history` once and derives the forward map with a private `retries_in(records, &history)` that `retries_by_job` is changed to call (same result). It returns empty at once when the job has no `retry_of` and no forward entry. Otherwise it walks forward to the newest standing retry, then back along `retry_of`, with a seen-set and `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` each way, and keeps jobs whose `records.jobs[id].state()` is Closed(Rejected | Failed | TimedOut), oldest first. `pub const LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT: usize = 3`. The batch `lineage_stops(records, jobs)` builds the history once and shares it across jobs.
decisions.reason: Reuses the one place the "try again on" form is read (`retried_job`, retry.rs:201). One history pass per ask, even for a whole queue. Finding 5 corrected: `retries_by_job` (retry.rs:253-265) skips retries closed without running (Dropped, Declined, Abandoned, Stale, Closed) and keeps a Queued retry as the newest standing retry, so the forward walk reaches a queued item, which is what the plan wants. `job_history` maps Stale to Failed (retry.rs:222), so the state is read from the record to keep stale out. TimedOut counts because `athena retry` and `RunStep::Failed.retry` treat it like rejected or failed.

decisions.choice: The replacement is an ordinary request built by `StewardRequest::new` and queued with `Athena::queue` (channel `cli`). Title `Re-scope or split <root id>: <first repeated item, one line, at most 80 characters>`. Body starts `Lineage <root id>: failed attempts <ids>.`, then the repeated findings (one line each, length-capped), then `Left for a later request:` for repeated items that did not fit. Acceptance is one bullet per repeated unmet criterion (`Meet: <criterion>`) and per repeated blocker/major finding (`Resolve: <summary>`), at most max(1, root bullets - 1) when the root has more than one bullet; never the root's full list. Files come from the repeated findings' locations (path with `:line[:col]` stripped, `looks_like_path`), kept to the root's `request_text_touches` when they overlap, else the root's, else `records/` (the fallback in `StewardRequest::from_change`, steward.rs:624-630). `lineage_stop` returns Queued(id) when a request job's text contains `Lineage <root id>:`, and Refused when the root request starts `Re-scope or split ` (the drain still stops; the operator decides).
decisions.reason: The narrowing is mechanical and checkable, so the cap is not laundered into a fresh allowance. `StewardRequest::new` checks the text against the parse `athena plan` uses and needs one bullet and one path, which the three-step files fallback guarantees. No new record type, so `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` are untouched.

decisions.choice: Close the tripping queued retry item with `Athena::close`, through a third `Steps` method `drop_stopped(&self, item, why) -> Result<bool, String>` (default `Ok(false)`). `RealSteps::drop_stopped` loads the records and closes only when the item's state is Queued and its own text is a `try again on` request (`retried_job` is Some); the reason names the narrower request. `Drain::narrow` calls it after a request exists (queued now or found by the marker), not for a Refused stop.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: the request says the narrower request is queued "in place of another retry" and the operator should no longer stop lineages by hand. `Athena::close` (crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs:74-109) closes a Queued or Proposed job as Dropped with a reason; my earlier claim that no path closes a queued request was wrong. A dropped item is skipped by `retries_by_job`, and `lineage_attempts` from any other member still counts the same three failed jobs, so the marker lookup still returns Queued. An item that already ran is not Queued, so nothing is closed for it. A close error becomes a note: the narrower request stays queued and the item is passed over as before.

rejected.option: Leave the item Queued for the operator to drop
rejected.why: Contradicts the request that the operator no longer acts by hand, and the item would be passed over on every run.
That path serves the hand `athena retry`.

decisions.choice: Once-per-lineage queuing is guarded in the drain's shared state, not only by the marker lookup. `State` gets `narrowed: BTreeMap<JobId, Result<String, String>>`. `Drain::narrow(item, &stop)` inserts the root in one critical section (check-and-insert on the `st()` mutex), releases the lock, calls `Steps::queue_narrower`, then stores the result; a second caller for the same root, including a worker of `drain_concurrent`, reads the stored result (or a note that another worker is queuing it) and does not queue. The mutex is not held across the `Steps` call. The result is kept for the run, including an error, so later waves do not retry or re-note it; the next run tries again.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: `lineage_stop` reads the marker from records, so two workers could both miss it before either commits. The drain's state is the place `carry` and `tried` already live. The marker lookup in `RealSteps` still covers a second run.

rejected.option: Rely on the marker lookup only
rejected.why: Two workers can both miss it before either commits.
It does a commit; other code in the drain does not hold the mutex across a `Steps` call.

decisions.choice: How a repeat is decided. Work on the structured data of each failed attempt's final verification: unmet criteria (criterion text) and blocker/major findings (`finding_blocks`; `summary`, `location`). Helpers in retry.rs: `location_path(loc)` strips trailing `:line` and `:line:col`. Unmet criteria: `same_criterion(a, b)` is `scope_guard::compare_criteria(a, b)` not `No` (scope_guard.rs:189-220), unchanged T4 behavior. Findings use a stricter `same_finding`: both located with equal `location_path` AND `same_summary`; or either unlocated AND `compare_criteria` is exactly `Yes`. `same_summary(a, b)` normalises with `normalise_criterion` (lowercase, digits dropped), splits on non-alphanumerics, drops a short fixed stop-word list (the, a, an, and, or, is, are, was, were, be, of, to, in, on, for, no, not, it, its, this, that, with, as, by, at, has, have) and then is true when the content-word lists are equal, or one list contains the other with at least 2 words, or at least 2 content words are shared and they are more than half of the shorter list. Items are clustered across attempts oldest first; a cluster seen in at least 2 distinct failed attempts is repeated and shows the latest wording. A failed attempt with no verification contributes its closing reason line. If nothing repeats, the last attempt's blocking findings are listed and the body says none repeated.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: `compare_criteria` returns Maybe when more than half of the shorter text's words are shared, stop words included (scope_guard.rs:212-216), so `Tests are missing` and `Docs are missing` (2 of 3 shared) would pair as one finding, and the cap on the request's size means a false repeat can push out a real one. With the stop-word list those two have content words {tests, missing} and {docs, missing}: 1 shared, not more than half, so they do not pair. Real fresh verifier runs add punctuation and line numbers (`The description lists no callers.` at `src/a.rs:10` vs `description lists no callers` at `src/a.rs:42`), which the normalisation, the word split and the path rule handle. For criteria the scope guard already trusts the T4 rule, and criteria in a lineage come from one acceptance list.

rejected.why: Rarely matches across independent verifier runs.

rejected.option: `compare_criteria` Maybe counts as a repeat for findings
rejected.why: Stop-word overlap pairs different short findings (finding 4).

risks.risk: The narrower request may be worked in a later wave of the same run with the one spare job (the plan is rebuilt before each wave, drain.rs:3022-3025) and add a job that looks like an extra attempt, in tests (A) and (C).
risks.mitigation: Tests assert on `lineage_attempts`, the marker count, the absence of a job `try again on <last>` and the passed-over line, never on the job total. The fake script answers any number of invocations by role, so an extra job closes Rejected without panic and starts its own lineage at zero. In (B) nothing else is worked: the queue is empty after the hold, so the invocation count is exact.

risks.risk: Dropping the tripping queued item with `Athena::close` could fail (job lock, config load) or drop an item the operator wanted kept.
risks.mitigation: Only a Queued item whose own text is a `try again on` request is closed, and the Dropped reason names the narrower request that replaces it. A close error becomes a note; the narrower request stays queued and the item is passed over. A hand `athena retry` can start the lineage again at any time.

risks.risk: A read-ahead or a concurrent worker could touch an item of a lineage that reaches 3 failures while it is in flight, since the earlier loop-top check is removed.
risks.mitigation: `prepare` is rebuilt before every wave and point 2 stops an item at its own failure; the `narrowed` guard ensures one request per lineage. Unverified: whether the plan can put two items of one lineage in one concurrent wave; if it could, each stops at its own failure, so the worst case is one extra in-flight attempt. The drain's shared state, not the records, is what the guard reads, and unit test (d) covers it.

risks.risk: The repeat match is too loose or too tight, so the request lists the wrong items.
risks.mitigation: Findings use the stricter stop-word rule and need equal paths; unlocated findings need a Yes; a miss falls back to the last attempt's blocking findings labeled as not repeated. Unit tests cover a renumbered and reworded repeat (must match) and unrelated summaries, different paths and the `Tests/Docs are missing` pair (must not match).

risks.risk: The narrower request could be as large as its root when the root has one bullet, or a narrower request could itself fail 3 times and be re-narrowed forever.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance is only the repeated items, capped strictly below the root's bullet count when it has several. A request whose root is a `Re-scope or split ` request gets Refused (nothing queued, nothing dropped, the drain still stops); a unit test covers it.

risks.risk: The last files fallback (`records/`) is weak for a code request.
risks.mitigation: It is reached only when neither the repeated findings' locations nor the root request name a path. It keeps the request buildable so a replacement is always queued, and a unit test covers the case.

risks.risk: Finding text may hold a boundary word or secret.
risks.mitigation: `StewardRequest::new` rewords boundary words and `Athena::queue` redacts. If queuing still errors, the drain holds or stops the lineage anyway, dispatches no 4th attempt and notes the error.

risks.risk: A lineage longer than `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` (16) or with a cycle.
risks.mitigation: Both walks use a seen-set and the same depth bound as `earlier_jobs`. A unit test covers a cyclic request. Past 16 hops the count is still at least 3, so the stop holds.

risks.risk: The reader's view of `buy-first` is shorter.
risks.mitigation: Only its first sentence is shown to the reader; the producer and verifier briefs still carry the whole statement. The CHANGELOG and change description name it as a behavior change, and the open question asks the user to confirm.
